ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening for all directors, officers, and ultimate beneficial owners against the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, Canada's Consolidated Canadian Autonomous Sanctions List (CASL), the Special Economic Measures Act sanctions lists, and the OFAC SDN List. Enhanced due diligence is required for politically exposed persons under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act and FINTRAC guidance, including establishment of source of funds and senior management approval. Continuous monitoring during the pre-incorporation stage and until onward corporate obligations lapse. Canadian sanctions screening must be completed before filing name clearance and again immediately before registration.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Alberta Corporate Registry – Corporate Name Search using the NUANS automated name search system, accessible through licensed Alberta Registry Agents and the online corporate registry portal available at alberta.ca/corporate-registry
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names must be expressed in Latin characters; English and French accents are permitted. The legal name of an Alberta unlimited liability corporation must contain the designator 'ULC' or 'Unlimited Liability Company', and non-Latin script names must be transliterated into English for registration. The registered Latin-script form is the operative legal name.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon name rejection, request a written decision from the Alberta Corporate Registry; file a reconsideration request through a licensed registry agent within 30 days of refusal, attaching the original NUANS report, a written explanation demonstrating non-confusion, and any required consent from the conflicting name holder. If reconsideration fails, an application may be made to the Court of King's Bench of Alberta under the Business Corporations Act for a court order approving the proposed name. Extension of a valid reservation is obtained by filing a fresh name reservation or re-running a NUANS search before the existing reservation expires.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not permitted as the statutory registered office; Alberta requires a physical service address within Alberta. A virtual office may be used for operational or mail-forwarding purposes only and cannot satisfy the Business Corporations Act registered office requirement.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low; estimated maximum 2% per calendar year for an unlicensed, low-risk hyper-casual mobile game publishing entity absent complaints, sanctions flags, or tax non-compliance triggers.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act (Alberta), RSA 2000, c. B-9, ss. 5-9, 12-13, 16, 18, 21, 101, 102, 124-126; applicable provisions of the Alberta Electronic Transactions Act for online filings.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry, Service Alberta and Red Tape Reduction, Government of Alberta; filings accepted electronically through accredited Registry Agents or the MyAlberta Business Link portal.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation under the Business Corporations Act (Alberta); issuance of Certificate of Incorporation by the Alberta Corporate Registry.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up share capital is prescribed under the Alberta Business Corporations Act; shares may be issued for any lawful consideration fixed by the directors, or credited as paid up under the articles. No escrow account is required by statute as a precondition to incorporation for an Alberta unlimited liability corporation.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: That the Articles of Incorporation and any applicable unanimous shareholder agreement are adopted; That the subscription for shares set out in the incorporation application is accepted and the shares are issued in accordance with the articles; That the registered office is fixed as [Legal Address], Alberta, with [Individual] appointed as registered office records officer; That the persons named in the Director Consent are appointed as first directors holding office until the first annual meeting; That [Name] is appointed President, [Name] is appointed Secretary, and [Name] is appointed Treasurer until removed by the Board; That banking resolutions and signing authorities are approved; and That management shall complete all post-registration corporate filings and municipal licences.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry through Service Alberta; NUANS pre-screen administered by accredited registry service providers.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a NUANS name search request for the proposed corporate name, including a distinct element and the required ULC designation variant. Obtain the NUANS report and, if available, contain name reservation number. Verify the name does not conflict with existing trademarks or corporate names and is otherwise permissible for an unlimited liability corporation.
required_dossiers: Proposed corporate name with ULC designation
Request letter or online application generated by the registry agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused, obtain a new NUANS report with a modified distinct element and resubmit. The registry will provide a deficiency notice; a corrected filing may be refiled without forfeiture of ministerial fees in most cases if done within the cure period prescribed by the registry.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Execution of Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry, Service Alberta and Red Tape Reduction; may be filed by the incorporator or through an accredited registry agent.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Articles of Incorporation in the prescribed form, specifying the corporate name with ULC element, registered office in Alberta, first director information, share structure, and any restrictions on share transfers or business activities. The incorporator must sign the articles. Include the signed consent to act as director for each named director.
required_dossiers: Registered office address and documents supporting office location, if any
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried for defective signatures or missing director consents, the registry will issue a deficiency notice. The applicant must correct the identified items and resubmit within the stated cure window; a new payment may be required only if the original filing is deemed fully rejected.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of Articles and Issuance of Certificate of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry, Service Alberta; electronic filing through MyAlberta Business Link or approved registry agent.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the completed Articles of Incorporation and all attachments electronically, or through a registry agent. Pay the applicable registration fee. Upon approval, the Corporate Registry will issue a Certificate of Incorporation together with a unique Alberta corporate access number. Confirm the registered office information and director details as noted in the registry extract.
required_dossiers: NUANS report and name reservation reference
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If incorporation is denied or delayed, the registry will issue a written rejection with reasons. The applicant may appeal administratively or refile with corrected articles within the statutory limitation period; if the rejection arose from a name conflict, a new name search and resubmission is required.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Organizational Meeting, By-laws, and Corporate Records
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors of the ULC; internal governance, subject to Alberta Corporate Registry statutory record-keeping rules.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first directors' meeting or execute circulating written resolutions. Adopt by-laws, issue share certificates, open corporate bank accounts, designate banking signatories, and register the minute book address and registered office records keeper as required under the Business Corporations Act (Alberta). File any required director information with the registry.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: No external administrative remedy applies; any omission in statutory records should be corrected by supplemental board resolutions and a charter document amendment if required. If director information was not timely filed with the registry, file a late correction and pay any late fee prescribed by the registry.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Incorporation Tax and Municipal Business Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency; municipal business licensing department for the City of Calgary, City of Edmonton, or other Alberta municipality; Alberta Corporate Registry for annual reporting.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the ULC with the Canada Revenue Agency for a Business Number, and apply for GST/HST, payroll, and corporate income tax accounts as applicable to the mobile games publishing activity. If occupying physical premises, apply to the local municipality for a general business licence and obtain any zoning or building occupancy approval. Also file the initial annual return with the Alberta Corporate Registry if required within the first year.
required_dossiers: Lease or ownership documentation for registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the municipal business licence is refused due to zoning or land-use restrictions, revise the application or select a compliant premises; provide evidence of compliance to the licensing authority. For CRA account delays, follow the CRA service complaint protocol and file an amended request; late annual returns can be cured by filing with interest or penalties if applicable.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: No Alberta provincial industrial manufacturing permit applies to software publishing; for physical office operations, the municipal licensing department of the city or municipal district where the gaming studio is located acts as the competent licensing authority.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: General Business Licence issued under the applicable Alberta municipal licensing by-law; alternatively, a Home Occupation Business Licence if the hyper-casual studio operates from a residential premises.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – Non-Scheduled Activity; software development and office-based game publishing do not trigger a full environmental impact assessment under the Environmental Protection and Enhancement Act, RSA 2000, c. E-12.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No process wastewater discharge; only sanitary flows permitted through municipal sewer. No VOC or hazardous air emissions from development activity; office waste, e-waste, batteries and electronic equipment must be handled under the Alberta Recycling Management Authority requirements and municipal solid waste bylaws.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety approval required under the Alberta Fire Code and National Fire Code, including geospatial fire route, extinguishers, and emergency lighting; occupancy permit from municipal building authority for structural load and life-safety compliance; Alberta OHS workplace hazard assessment, emergency response plan, and first-aid clearance required for employees.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) / Agence du revenu du Canada (ARC); registration portal: Business Registration Online (BRO) and My Business Account (MBA) at canada.ca/en/revenue-agency; GST/HST NETFILE for indirect tax returns
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: File Articles/Notice of Articles for the Alberta ULC through Corporate Registry; Step 2: Obtain the 9-digit Business Number (BN) via BRO online or Form RC1 (Request for a Business Number), which serves as the universal federal identifier; Step 3: Add program accounts as needed: RT (Corporate Income Tax), RT (GST/HST), RP (Payroll), RC (Excise Tax). For foreign-owned ULCs, CRA requires a Canadian resident director for GST/HST purposes? Actually no...

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada). Canada has no separate foreign-exchange control administrator; the Department of Finance Canada exercises residual exchange-policy authority under the Currency Act, OSFI supervises regulated financial institutions, and FINTRAC administers AML/CFT reporting.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada is an IMF Article VIII member and maintains full convertibility on both current and capital account. There are no exchange-control permits, conversion approvals, or surrender requirements restricting CAD/USD/EUR flows for dividends, royalties, loan repayments, or capital repatriation. The operative hurdles are tax-based: non-resident remittances are subject to Part XIII withholding taxes (generally 25% absent treaty relief), and intercompany settlements must satisfy arm's length, anti-deferral, and thin-capitalization rules. Routine profit distributions may be made freely, but the paying Canadian bank will expect the ULC to demonstrate withholding compliance and to provide tax-residence forms so that the bank is protected under the Income Tax Act.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Canada imposes no statutory timeline for repatriation and no mandatory conversion ratio for export proceeds or cross-border service revenue. Receipts may be retained in foreign currency. For AML purposes, physical currency and monetary instruments of C$10,000 or more entering or leaving Canada must be reported to CBSA/FINTRAC, and large virtual-currency transactions must also be reported. Digital-games export revenue should nevertheless be evidenced by ad-network payout reports for bank, FINTRAC, and CRA audit purposes.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low-to-Medium as a primary treasury channel. Canada does not grant offshore digital EMIs bank-deposit authority, and an unlicensed EMI cannot act as a primary CAD clearing member via Lynx or ACSS. An overseas EMI may be used only as a supplementary payout gateway for USD/EUR ad-network proceeds, provided the entity is licensed in its home state, registered in Canada as an MSB if it carries on money-services business in Canada, and maintains segregated client funds. The ULC should keep its principal operating and reserve balances in a Schedule I bank or a fully authorized foreign-bank branch to avoid FINTRAC, OSFI, and Payments Canada concerns.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: There is no federal statutory mandate that all directors appear physically in Canada. FINTRAC permits remote identification through verified digital credential, video call, and credit-file matching, and Canadian banks commonly onboard non-resident ULC shareholders remotely. In practice, Schedule I banks typically require at least one principal director, compliance officer, or authorized signatory to attend either an in-branch interview or a comprehensive video KYC interview, and a Canadian resident agent or registered office is mandatory for the Alberta ULC. Documents executed by non-resident directors must be notarized and, where required, apostilled before the bank will accept the mandate.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident shareholders or ultimate beneficial owners located in jurisdictions with weak CDD frameworks, high-risk sectors, or sanctions exposure
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized passports, proof of residential address, professional bank references from the home institution, FINTRAC/OFAC/UN sanctions screening results, source-of-funds and source-of-wealth declarations, corporate-chain organigram, and a legal opinion confirming no sanctioned person controls the ULC.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unlimited Liability Company structure used with nominee shareholders, bearer-share-like arrangements, or multi-layer hybrid ownership creating beneficial-ownership opacity
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete Alberta beneficial-ownership registry filing, current shareholder register, register of significant individuals, ULC declaration or operating agreement, trust deeds or voting agreements, check-the-box election analysis for US tax, and a Canadian legal opinion describing ultimate control.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Projected high-volume ad-network inflows from AdMob and AppLovin without documented commercial substance or verifiable transaction history
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed publisher agreements with Google Ireland and AppLovin, app-store ownership registration, ad-performance dashboards, historical payout statements from AdMob_Payout and AppLovin_Payout rails, 12-month revenue forecast, and intercompany/transfer-pricing documentation consistent with the ISIC 5820 software-publishing scope.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Request for immediate outbound disbursements to non-resident related parties, contractors, or royalty holders before the account relationship has matured
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Board-approved treasury payment policy, intercompany agreements with arm's length pricing, Part XIII withholding analysis, W-8BEN-E or NR301 forms, NR4/T106 filing history, invoices and statements of work, and a pre-cleared expected-counterparty schedule reviewed by bank compliance.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Cross-border capital injections from the non-resident parent or subscribers should be effected by SWIFT MT103 or, for domestic CAD, by Bank of Canada Lynx wire to the ULC's operating account. The receiving bank will require the corporate resolution, updated share register, source-of-wealth evidence, and a remittance narrative classifying the funds as equity (for example, capital contribution to share capital under a subscription agreement) or evidenced debt (shareholder loan with executed promissory note). Canada has no central-bank approval code, but the bank's compliance team expects an MT103/ISO 20022 purpose descriptor matching the underlying transaction. To avoid deemed-dividend characterization and Part XIII withholding, inbound funds must not be described merely as owner advance; contemporaneous legal and tax documentation must support the chosen capital structure. USD injections should be pre-routed through the bank's U.S. correspondent via Fedwire or CHIPS, and any CAD conversion should be priced under the treasury's FX policy.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound disbursements are unencumbered by exchange controls. CAD vendor payments may be settled through Payments Canada ACSS in batch or through Lynx for high-value time-critical wires. International settlements should use SWIFT MT103 to the beneficiary bank, routed through the correspondent banking network; for USD, the ULC may use an internal USD ledger with Fedwire/CHIPS clearing, and the bank may offer commercial LC facilities for documentary trade if a counterparty insists. For a hyper-casual games publisher, commercial LCs are typically unnecessary because AdMob and AppLovin payouts are electronic receivables, not documentary trade. Payments of royalties, management fees, or interest to non-residents require contemporaneous Part XIII withholding and NR4/T106 filings; the clearing bank may condition execution on receiving the withholding analysis and beneficiary tax forms. The treasury ledger should tag AdMob_Payout and AppLovin_Payout collections separately and reconcile each rail against platform statements to satisfy bank monitoring and CRA audit readiness.

Spot and tomorrow-next (tom-next) FX swaps for day-to-day liquidity and rollover management
